title.zh: 卷一百六十一 列傳第四十八: 楊大淵 劉整
title.en: Volume 161 Biographies 48: Yang Dayuan, Liu Zheng
title.raw: 卷一百六十一 列傳第四十八: 楊大淵 劉整 Volume 161 Biographies 48: Yang Dayuan, Liu Zheng

sentences.zh: 楊大淵文安附

translations.literal: Yang Dayuan, with Wen'an appended
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayuan (with biography of Wen'an appended)

sentences.zh: 楊大淵，天水人也。

translations.literal: Yang Dayuan was a native of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayuan came from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 與兄大全、弟大楫，皆仕宋。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Daquan and younger brother Daqi all served the Song.
translations.idiomatic: He, his elder brother Daquan, and his younger brother Daqi all held office under the Song.

sentences.zh: 大淵緫兵守閬州。

translations.literal: Dayuan commanded troops garrisoning Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan held overall military command at Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，憲宗兵至閬州之大獲城，遣宋降臣王仲入招大淵，大淵殺之。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu, Emperor Xianzong's army reached Dahuocheng in Lang Prefecture; he sent the Song defector Wang Zhong to enter and summon Dayuan, and Dayuan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year (1258), the armies of Emperor Xianzong (Möngke) reached Dahuocheng in Langzhou; he sent the Song turncoat Wang Zhong to negotiate Dayuan's surrender, but Dayuan had him killed.

sentences.zh: 憲宗怒，督諸軍力攻，大淵懼，遂以城降。

translations.literal: Xianzong was enraged and urged the armies to attack with full force; Dayuan was afraid and thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xianzong pressed all his forces in a fierce assault; Dayuan, in fear, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 憲宗命誅之，汪田哥諫止，乃免。

translations.literal: Xianzong ordered him executed; Wang Tiange remonstrated and stopped it, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong ordered him put to death, but Wang Tiange intervened and persuaded him to desist, so Dayuan was spared.

sentences.zh: 命以其兵從，招降蓬、廣安諸郡，進攻釣魚山。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow with his troops, receive the surrender of Peng and Guang'an and other commanderies, and advance to attack Diaoyu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to march with his troops, accept the submission of Peng, Guang'an, and other districts, and press the attack on Diaoyushan.

sentences.zh: 擢大楫為管軍緫管，從諸王攻禮義城。

translations.literal: Daqi was promoted to commander-in-chief of army management and followed the princes in attacking Liyi City.
translations.idiomatic: Daqi was promoted to commander of army administration and joined the imperial princes in the assault on Liyi City.

sentences.zh: 己未冬，拜大淵侍郎、都行省，悉以閫外之寄委之。

translations.literal: In the winter of jiwei, Dayuan was appointed Vice Minister and Pacification Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat; all responsibilities beyond the passes were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei winter (1259), Dayuan was appointed Vice Minister and Pacification Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat, with full authority over affairs beyond the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 先是，大淵建言，謂取吳必先取蜀，取蜀必先據夔，乃遣其姪文安攻宋巴渠。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dayuan had offered counsel, saying that to take Wu one must first take Shu, and to take Shu one must first hold Kui; he thereupon sent his nephew Wen'an to attack Ba and Qu in Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Dayuan had advised that conquering Wu required first conquering Shu, and conquering Shu required first securing Kui; he then dispatched his nephew Wen'an to attack the Song districts of Ba and Qu.

sentences.zh: 至萬安寨，守將盧埴降。

translations.literal: When they reached Wan'an Stockade, the defending commander Lu Zhi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Wan'an Stockade the defending officer Lu Zhi submitted.

sentences.zh: 復使文安相夔、達要衝，城蟠龍山。

translations.literal: He again had Wen'an survey the strategic passes of Kui and Da and fortify Panlong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Wen'an to reconnoiter the vital passes of Kui and Da and build a fortress on Panlong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 山四面巖阻，可以進攻退守，城未畢，宋夔路提刑鄭子發曰：「蟠龍，夔之咽喉，使敵得據之，則夔難守矣，此必爭之地也。」

translations.literal: The mountain was precipitous on all four sides, suitable for attack and defense; before the fort was finished, the Song Kui Circuit investigating commissioner Zheng Zifa said: 'Panlong is the throat of Kui; if the enemy holds it, Kui will be hard to defend—this is ground that must be contested.'
translations.idiomatic: Steep cliffs ringed the mountain on every side, ideal for offensive and defensive operations. Before the fort was complete, the Song investigating commissioner of the Kui circuit, Zheng Zifa, said: 'Panlong is the throat of Kui; if the enemy secures it, Kui cannot be held. This is ground that must be fought for.'

sentences.zh: 遂率兵來爭。

translations.literal: " He thereupon led troops to contest it.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his forces to dispute the position.

sentences.zh: 大安悉力備禦，大淵聞有宋兵，即遣姪安撫使文仲將兵往援。

translations.literal: Da'an made full preparations for defense; when Dayuan heard Song troops had come, he immediately sent his nephew, Pacification Commissioner Wenzhong, to lead troops to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Da'an made every preparation for defense. When Dayuan learned Song forces were approaching, he at once dispatched his nephew, Pacification Commissioner Wenzhong, with troops to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 宋兵宵遁，追敗之。

translations.literal: The Song army fled by night; they pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song troops fled under cover of night; the pursuers routed them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，詔以大淵麾下將士有功，賜金符十、銀符十九，別給海青符二，俾事亟則馳以聞，其後賞合州之功，復賜白金五十兩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, an edict awarded Dayuan's subordinate officers and soldiers who had merit: ten gold tally-tokens and nineteen silver tally-tokens, with two special 'sea eagle' tally-tokens besides, so that when affairs were urgent they might gallop to report; later, for merit at He Prefecture, fifty taels of white silver were also granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an edict rewarded the meritorious officers and men under Dayuan with ten gold tally-tokens and nineteen silver tally-tokens, plus two special sea-eagle tally-tokens for urgent reporting to court. Later, for achievements at Hezhou, fifty taels of white silver were added.

sentences.zh: 大淵欲於利州大安軍以鹽易軍糧，請于朝，從之。

translations.literal: Dayuan wished to exchange salt for army grain at Da'an Military Prefecture in Lizhou and requested permission from court; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan proposed trading salt for military grain at Da'an Army in Lizhou and petitioned the court, which approved.

sentences.zh: 冬，大淵入覲，拜東川都元帥，俾與征南都元帥欽察同署事。

translations.literal: In winter Dayuan came to audience and was appointed Marshal of the Eastern Chuan Pacification Commission, ordered to administer affairs jointly with the Southern Campaign Marshal Qincha.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Dayuan presented himself at court and was appointed Marshal of the Eastern Chuan Pacification Commission, sharing administration with the Southern Campaign Marshal Qincha.

sentences.zh: 大淵還，復於渠江濱築虎嘯城，以逼宋大良城，不踰時而就。

translations.literal: When Dayuan returned, he again built Huxiao City on the banks of the Qu River to press Song's Daliang City; it was completed in no time.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Dayuan built Huxiao City on the Qu River to threaten the Song fortress of Daliang, finishing it in short order.

sentences.zh: 四年，宋賈似道遣楊琳齎空名告身及蠟書、金幣，誘大淵南歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Song minister Jia Sidao sent Yang Lin bearing blank commissions, wax-sealed letters, gold, and coins to lure Dayuan back to the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Song minister Jia Sidao sent Yang Lin with blank appointment documents, wax-sealed dispatches, gold, and cash to entice Dayuan to rejoin the Song.

sentences.zh: 文安擒之以聞，詔誅琳。

translations.literal: Wen'an captured him and reported; an edict ordered Lin executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an seized him and reported to court; an edict ordered Lin put to death.

sentences.zh: 五月，世祖以大淵及張大悅復神山功，詔獎諭，仍賜蒙古、漢軍鈔百錠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Founder (Kublai) because of Dayuan's and Zhang Dayue's merit in recovering Shen Mountain issued a commendatory edict and also granted one hundred ingots of Mongol and Han army paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Founder, for Dayuan's and Zhang Dayue's recovery of Shen Mountain, issued a reward edict and granted one hundred ingots of Mongol and Han army banknotes.

sentences.zh: 子文粲，襲為閬蓬廣安順慶夔府等路都元帥。

translations.literal: His son Wencan succeeded as Marshal of Lang, Peng, Guang'an, Shunqing, Kuifu, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wencan inherited the post of Marshal of Lang, Peng, Guang'an, Shunqing, Kuifu, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 兄子文安。

translations.literal: His brother's son Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: His brother's son Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 文安字泰叔，父大全，仕宋守敘州。

translations.literal: Wen'an, courtesy name Taishu; his father was Daquan, who served the Song as defender of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an, style Taishu, was the son of Daquan, who had served the Song as prefect of Xu.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，國兵入蜀，大全戰死，贈武節大夫、眉州防禦使，諡愍忠，官其長子文仲。

translations.literal: In renyin the national armies entered Shu; Daquan died in battle. He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Martial Integrity and Defender of Mei Prefecture, with the posthumous title Minzhong; his eldest son Wenzhong was given office.
translations.idiomatic: In renyin (1242) the imperial armies entered Shu. Daquan fell in battle and was posthumously made Grand Master of Martial Integrity and Defender of Mei, with the posthumous title Minzhong; his eldest son Wenzhong received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 文安方二歲，母劉氏鞠之，依叔父大淵于閬州。

translations.literal: Wen'an was then two years old; his mother, Lady Liu, reared him and relied on his uncle Dayuan at Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an was only two; his mother, Lady Liu, raised him and lived under his uncle Dayuan at Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊午，憲宗以兵攻大獲，大淵以郡降，授侍郎、都行省，文仲亦授安撫使。

translations.literal: In wuwu, Xianzong attacked Dahu with troops; Dayuan surrendered the commandery and was appointed Vice Minister and Pacification Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat; Wenzhong was also appointed Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In wuwu (1258) Xianzong attacked Dahu. Dayuan surrendered the prefecture and was made Vice Minister and Pacification Commissioner of the Branch Secretariat; Wenzhong was also made Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，改授金符，仍前職，還攻宋開、達等州，擒其統制張剛、緫管伏林。

translations.literal: In the second year he was reassigned the gold tally-token while retaining his former post; returning, he attacked Song Kai, Da, and other prefectures and captured their commanders Zhang Gang and Supervisor Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he received a gold tally-token while keeping his former duties. On campaign he took the Song prefectures of Kai and Da and captured the commanders Zhang Gang and Supervisor Fulin.

sentences.zh: 八月，宋兵由開州運糧餉達，文安率奇兵，間道邀擊之，獲緫管方富等。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Song troops transported grain from Kai Prefecture to supply Da; Wen'an led picked troops by a hidden route to intercept them and captured Supervisor Fang Fu and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Song forces shipped grain from Kaizhou to Da. Wen'an led picked troops along a bypath, ambushed the convoy, and took Supervisor Fang Fu and others.

sentences.zh: 行省上其功，命充夔東路征行元帥，令以前後所俘入見。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat reported his merit; he was ordered to serve as Campaign Marshal of the Eastern Kui Route and commanded to present himself with all captives taken before and after.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat memorialized his achievements; he was appointed Campaign Marshal of the Eastern Kui Route and ordered to appear at court with his prisoners, past and present.

sentences.zh: 詔賜黃金、鞍馬有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted gold, saddles, and horses in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded gold, saddles, and horses in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 還，攻奪宋金州斷虎隘，殺其將梁富，擒路鈐、趙貴等。

translations.literal: On his return he attacked and seized the Song Jin Prefecture pass Duanhu'ai, killed their general Liang Fu, and captured Route Controller Zhao Gui and others.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he stormed the Song Jinzhou pass at Duanhu'ai, killed the general Liang Fu, and captured Route Controller Zhao Gui and others.

sentences.zh: 三年春，與千戶李吉等略開州之大通，與宋將硬弓張大戰，獲統制陳德等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, with the chiliarch Li Ji and others he raided Datong in Kai Prefecture, fought the Song general 'Hard Bow' Zhang, and captured Commander Chen De and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, with the chiliarch Li Ji and others he raided Datong in Kaizhou, fought the Song general Zhang the Hard Bow, and took Commander Chen De and others.

sentences.zh: 冬，緫帥汪惟正遣其將李木波等由間道襲開州，文安遣千戶王福引兵助之。

translations.literal: In winter the supreme commander Wang Weizheng sent his generals Li Mubo and others by a hidden route to strike Kai Prefecture; Wen'an sent the chiliarch Wang Fu with troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the supreme commander Wang Weizheng sent Li Mubo and others along a concealed route against Kaizhou; Wen'an dispatched the chiliarch Wang Fu to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 福先登，破其城，宋將龐彥海投崖死，擒副將劉安仁，留兵戍其地。

translations.literal: Fu was first to scale the walls and broke the city; the Song general Pang Yanhai threw himself from a cliff and died; the deputy commander Liu Anren was captured and troops were left to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu led the assault, breached the walls first, and took the city. The Song general Pang Yanhai leaped from a cliff to his death; Deputy Commander Liu Anren was captured and a garrison was left behind.

sentences.zh: 宋諸路兵來救，圍城三匝，築壘城外，文安密遣人入城，諭以堅守。

translations.literal: Song forces from various routes came to relieve the siege, encircling the city three deep and building ramparts outside; Wen'an secretly sent men into the city to urge steadfast defense.
translations.idiomatic: Song troops from several circuits arrived to relieve the siege, ringing the city threefold and erecting outer ramparts. Wen'an secretly sent men inside to urge them to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 四年春，行省命文安往援，即率兵斷其糧道，宋兵戰甚力，飛矢中文安面，拔矢力戰，大破之，殺其將張德等。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Branch Secretariat ordered Wen'an to reinforce; he immediately led troops to cut their grain route. The Song army fought fiercely; a flying arrow struck Wen'an in the face—he pulled it out and fought on, routing them and killing their general Zhang De and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year the Branch Secretariat ordered Wen'an to the relief. He led troops to sever the enemy supply line. The Song fought fiercely; a stray arrow struck Wen'an in the face—he drew it out, pressed the attack, broke them utterly, and killed their general Zhang De and others.

sentences.zh: 二月，文安以創甚，還蟠龍，宋兵遂復開州。

translations.literal: In the second month, because his wounds were severe, Wen'an returned to Panlong; the Song army thereupon recovered Kai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month his wounds were grave and Wen'an withdrew to Panlong; the Song then retook Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 文安乃遣緫把馬才、楊彪掠達州盧灘峽，與宋兵遇，擒其將蒲德。

translations.literal: Wen'an then sent the company commanders Ma Cai and Yang Biao to raid Luzhan Gorge in Da Prefecture; encountering Song troops, they captured their general Pu De.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an then sent company commanders Ma Cai and Yang Biao to raid Luzhan Gorge in Dazhou; meeting Song forces, they captured the general Pu De.

sentences.zh: 五年，文仲卒，詔文安就佩金虎符，充閬州夔東路安撫使軍民元帥，仍相副都元帥府事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wenzhong died; an edict ordered Wen'an to wear the gold tiger tally on the spot as Pacification Commissioner and Military-Civilian Marshal of the Eastern Kui Route at Lang, still assisting the deputy marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Wenzhong died. An edict had Wen'an assume the gold tiger tally as Pacification Commissioner and Military-Civilian Marshal of the Eastern Kui Route at Langzhou, while continuing to assist the deputy marshal's command.

sentences.zh: 閬州累遭兵變，戶口凋耗，文安乃教以耕桑，鰥寡不能自存，願相配偶者，併為一戶充役，民始復業。

translations.literal: Lang Prefecture had repeatedly suffered military upheaval and its population was depleted; Wen'an taught them farming and sericulture. Widows and widowers unable to support themselves who wished to be matched were registered as one household for corvée, and the people began to recover their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhou had suffered repeated turmoil and its households were depleted. Wen'an promoted farming and sericulture; widows and widowers who wished to marry were combined into single households for corvée service, and the people gradually returned to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 冬，遣千戶馬才、張琪略達州，擒宋將范伸、王德、解明等。

translations.literal: In winter he sent the chiliarchs Ma Cai and Zhang Qi to raid Da Prefecture and captured the Song generals Fan Shen, Wang De, and Xie Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he sent the chiliarchs Ma Cai and Zhang Qi against Dazhou and captured the Song generals Fan Shen, Wang De, and Xie Ming.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣蔡邦光、李吉、嵇永興，略達州之朱師鄭巿，擒緫管周德新、裨將王遷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he sent Cai Bangguang, Li Ji, and Ji Yongxing to raid Zhushizheng Market in Da Prefecture and captured Supervisor Zhou Dexin and the deputy Wang Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he sent Cai Bangguang, Li Ji, and Ji Yongxing against Zhushizheng market in Dazhou, taking Supervisor Zhou Dexin and Deputy Wang Qian.

sentences.zh: 秋，遣緫把王顯略達州之泥埧，擒緫管張威。

translations.literal: In autumn he sent the company commander Wang Xian to raid Niba in Da Prefecture and captured Supervisor Zhang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he sent the company commander Wang Xian against Niba in Dazhou and captured Supervisor Zhang Wei.

sentences.zh: 冬，遣兵掠大寧之曲水，擒副將王仁。

translations.literal: In winter he sent troops to raid Qushui in Daning and captured the deputy Wang Ren.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he sent troops against Qushui in Daning and took the deputy Wang Ren.

sentences.zh: 七年，從嚴僉省攻重慶，大戰于龍坎，敗宋兵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Commissioner Yan in attacking Chongqing; a great battle was fought at Longkan and the Song army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Commissioner Yan's assault on Chongqing; at Longkan a major battle ended in defeat for the Song.

sentences.zh: 攻鏵鐵寨，擒其將袁宜、何世賢等。

translations.literal: They attacked Huatie Stockade and captured the generals Yuan Yi, He Shixian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Huatie Stockade and captured the generals Yuan Yi, He Shixian, and others.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔賜白金、寶鈔、幣帛有差。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an edict granted white silver, treasure notes, and silks in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Victory was reported to court; an edict granted white silver, treasure notes, and silks in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 秋，攻達州之聖耳城，擒宋將楊普、時仲，芟其禾而還。

translations.literal: In autumn they attacked the Song Shen'er City in Da Prefecture, captured the Song generals Yang Pu and Shi Zhong, cut down their grain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn they attacked Shen'er City in Dazhou, captured the Song generals Yang Pu and Shi Zhong, destroyed the standing grain, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又遣元帥蔡邦光略開州，擒宋將陳俊。

translations.literal: He again sent Marshal Cai Bangguang to raid Kai Prefecture and captured the Song general Chen Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Marshal Cai Bangguang against Kaizhou and captured the Song general Chen Jun.

sentences.zh: 冬，文粲入見，帝諭之曰：「汝兄弟宣力邊陲，朕所知也。」

translations.literal: In winter Wencan came to audience; the Emperor addressed him: 'Your brothers have exerted themselves on the frontier—I am well aware of it.'
translations.idiomatic: In winter Wencan presented himself at court. The Emperor told him: 'Your brothers have served with distinction on the border; I know it well.'

sentences.zh: 進文安階為明威將軍。

translations.literal: Wen'an was advanced in rank to General of Illustrious Might.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an was promoted to General of Illustrious Might.

sentences.zh: 八年春，遣蔡邦光攻達州，戰于聖耳城下，擒其將蒲桂。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he sent Cai Bangguang to attack Da Prefecture; fighting below Shen'er City, he captured the general Pu Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he sent Cai Bangguang against Dazhou; below Shen'er City he captured the general Pu Gui.

sentences.zh: 又戰開州之沙平，擒其將王順。

translations.literal: He again fought at Shaping in Kai Prefecture and captured the general Wang Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Shaping in Kaizhou and took the general Wang Shun.

sentences.zh: 時宋以朱禩孫帥蜀，禩孫，閬人也，數遣間諜，動搖人心，文安屢獲其諜，閬州竟無虞。

translations.literal: At that time the Song appointed Zhu Xiansun to command Shu; Xiansun was a native of Lang and repeatedly sent spies to shake popular loyalty, but Wen'an captured his agents again and again, and Lang Prefecture remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had appointed Zhu Xiansun to command in Shu. A Lang native, Xiansun repeatedly sent spies to undermine loyalty, but Wen'an captured them repeatedly and Langzhou remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，文安會東川統軍匣剌攻達州，三戰三捷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Wen'an joined the Eastern Chuan commander-in-chief Hulai in attacking Da Prefecture; three battles, three victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wen'an joined the Eastern Chuan commander Hulai against Dazhou—three engagements, three victories.

sentences.zh: 尋遣千戶嵇永興攻開州，戰于平、曲水，擒緫管王道等。

translations.literal: Soon he sent the chiliarch Ji Yongxing to attack Kai Prefecture; fighting at Pingyang and Qushui, he captured Supervisor Wang Dao and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent the chiliarch Ji Yongxing against Kaizhou; at Pingyang and Qushui he captured Supervisor Wang Dao and others.

sentences.zh: 軍還，以所俘入見，帝深加獎諭，擢昭勇大將軍、東川路征南招討使，賜金銀、寶鈔、鞍馬、弓矢、幣帛有差。

translations.literal: When the army returned he presented captives at audience; the Emperor praised him deeply, promoting him to Grand General of Valiant Courage and Southern Campaign Commissioner of the Eastern Chuan Route, granting gold, silver, treasure notes, saddles, horses, bows, arrows, and silks in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented prisoners at court. The Emperor commended him warmly, promoting him to Grand General of Valiant Courage and Southern Campaign Commissioner of the Eastern Chuan Route, with gold, silver, treasure notes, saddles, horses, bows, arrows, and silks in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，領軍出小寧，措置屯田，遣韓福攻達州九君山，擒宋將張俊。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year he led the army out to Xiaoning to organize garrison farming and sent Han Fu to attack Jiujun Mountain in Da Prefecture, capturing the Song general Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year he led troops to Xiaoning to establish military colonies and sent Han Fu against Jiujun Mountain in Dazhou, capturing the Song general Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 遣元帥蔡邦光會蓬州兵，邀宋師于永睦，戰勝之。

translations.literal: He sent Marshal Cai Bangguang to join Peng Prefecture troops and intercept Song forces at Yongmu, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Marshal Cai Bangguang with Pengzhou troops to intercept Song forces at Yongmu and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 復遣嵇永興、楊彪追襲宋裨將劉威等，破聖耳外城，獲寨主楊桂，縱兵焚掠而還。

translations.literal: He again sent Ji Yongxing and Yang Biao in pursuit of the Song deputy Liu Wei and others, broke the outer wall of Shen'er, took Stockade Chief Yang Gui, and returned after burning and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Ji Yongxing and Yang Biao in pursuit of the Song deputy Liu Wei and others, breached the outer works of Shen'er, took Stockade Chief Yang Gui, and withdrew after burning and looting.

sentences.zh: 九月，築金湯城，以積屯田之糧，且以逼宋龍爪城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he built Jintang City to store colony grain and to press Song's Longzhao City.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he built Jintang City to stock colony grain and threaten the Song fortress of Longzhao.

sentences.zh: 慮宋兵必來爭，遣韓福出兵通川，以牽制之，與宋兵遇于銼耳山，敗之，俘緫管蔡雲龍等。

translations.literal: Fearing Song troops would certainly contest it, he sent Han Fu with troops to Tong Prefecture as a diversion; they met Song forces at Cuo'er Mountain, defeated them, and captured Supervisor Cai Yunlong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting a Song counterattack, he sent Han Fu toward Tongzhou as a diversion. At Cuo'er Mountain they routed the Song and captured Supervisor Cai Yunlong and others.

sentences.zh: 出達州牛門，斷宋兵回路，擒緫管李佺、李德。

translations.literal: He went out through Niumen in Da Prefecture, cut the Song army's line of retreat, and captured Supervisors Li Quan and Li De.
translations.idiomatic: Marching out through Niumen in Dazhou, he severed the Song line of retreat and captured Supervisors Li Quan and Li De.

sentences.zh: 宋兵輸糧達州，遣兵于盧灘峽邀擊之，擒統制孫聰、張順等。

translations.literal: When Song troops transported grain to Da Prefecture, he sent troops to ambush them at Luzhan Gorge and captured Commanders Sun Cong and Zhang Shun and others.
translations.idiomatic: As Song convoys moved grain to Dazhou, he ambushed them at Luzhan Gorge and took Commanders Sun Cong and Zhang Shun and others.

sentences.zh: 夏，遣元帥李吉略開州，戰于瀉油坡，擒其提舉李貴，及石寨主雍德。

translations.literal: In summer he sent Marshal Li Ji to raid Kai Prefecture; fighting at Xieyou Slope, he captured their Commissioner Li Gui and the Shijie Stockade chief Yong De.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he sent Marshal Li Ji against Kaizhou; at Xieyou Slope he captured Commissioner Li Gui and the Shijie stockade chief Yong De.

sentences.zh: 宋兵復由羅頂山輸糧開、達，遣蔡邦光、李吉伏兵遮之，擒裨將吳金等，覆其糧船。

translations.literal: Song troops again transported grain to Kai and Da by Luoding Mountain; he sent Cai Bangguang and Li Ji with ambush troops to intercept, capturing the deputy Wu Jin and others and sinking their grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: Song convoys again moved supplies to Kai and Da via Luoding Mountain. Cai Bangguang and Li Ji lay in ambush, captured Deputy Wu Jin and others, and destroyed the grain fleet.

sentences.zh: 閏十月，蓬州兵攻拔龍爪城，東川統軍司命文安兼領之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary tenth month Peng Prefecture troops stormed Longzhao City; the Eastern Chuan commander-in-chief's office ordered Wen'an to take charge as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary tenth month Pengzhou troops took Longzhao City; the Eastern Chuan command ordered Wen'an to assume joint command.

sentences.zh: 時蓬州兵已去，宋都統趙章復來據之，且出兵迎敵，文安與戰，破之，擒緫管王元而還。

translations.literal: At that time the Peng troops had already withdrawn; the Song commander-in-chief Zhao Zhang came again to hold it and sallied to meet the enemy; Wen'an fought, defeated them, captured Supervisor Wang Yuan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Pengzhou force had already withdrawn when the Song commander-in-chief Zhao Zhang reoccupied Longzhao and marched out to engage. Wen'an broke them, captured Supervisor Wang Yuan, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋，宋都統閻國寶、監軍張應庚，運糧于達州，文安邀之于瀉油坡，奪其糧，并擒二將。

translations.literal: In autumn the Song commander-in-chief Yan Guobao and Supervisor Zhang Yinggeng transported grain to Da Prefecture; Wen'an intercepted them at Xieyou Slope, seized the grain, and captured both generals.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn the Song commander Yan Guobao and Supervisor Zhang Yinggeng convoyed grain to Dazhou. Wen'an intercepted them at Xieyou Slope, seized the supplies, and took both commanders.

sentences.zh: 宋開州守將鮮汝忠邀遮歸路，與戰敗之，獲緫轄秦興祖、譚友孫。

translations.literal: The Song defender of Kai Prefecture, Xian Ruzhong, blocked the return route; they fought and defeated him, capturing the controllers Qin Xingzu and Tan Yousun.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Kaizhou defender Xian Ruzhong barred the line of march; Wen'an defeated him and captured Controllers Qin Xingzu and Tan Yousun.

sentences.zh: 十一年春三月，文安率軍屯小寧，得俘者言，鮮汝忠等將取蟠龍之麥，即遣千戶王新德、楊彪等散掠宋境，文安自戍蟠龍以備之。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the eleventh year Wen'an led troops to garrison Xiaoning; from captives he learned that Xian Ruzhong and others intended to harvest Panlong's wheat, and immediately sent the chiliarchs Wang Xinde and Yang Biao to raid Song territory while he himself guarded Panlong in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eleventh year Wen'an encamped at Xiaoning. Prisoners reported that Xian Ruzhong and others meant to harvest Panlong's wheat; he at once sent the chiliarchs Wang Xinde and Yang Biao to raid Song territory while he held Panlong in person.

sentences.zh: 李吉略由山，戰于城下，擒其將葉勝。

translations.literal: Li Ji raided Youshan; fighting below the city, he captured the general Ye Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji raided Youshan; fighting below the walls he captured the general Ye Sheng.

sentences.zh: 遣蔡邦光、楊彪掠竹山寨，與趙統制戰，擒其將鄭桂、莊俊。

translations.literal: He sent Cai Bangguang and Yang Biao to raid Zhushan Stockade; fighting the Song commander Zhao, he captured the generals Zheng Gui and Zhuang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cai Bangguang and Yang Biao against Zhushan Stockade; engaging Commander Zhao of the Song, he took the generals Zheng Gui and Zhuang Jun.

sentences.zh: 秋，與蒙古漢軍萬戶怯必烈等，攻宋夔東，拔高陽、夔、巫等寨，擒守將嚴貴、竇世忠、趙興，因跨江為橋，以斷宋兵往來之路，宋兵來爭，戰却之。

translations.literal: In autumn, with the Mongol and Han army myriarch Qiebilei and others, he attacked eastern Kui in Song territory, took the stockades of Gaoyang, Kui, and Wu, and captured the defenders Yan Gui, Dou Shizhong, and Zhao Xing; they then spanned the river with a bridge to cut Song communications, and when Song troops came to contest it they were repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, with the Mongol-Han myriarch Qiebilei and others, he attacked eastern Kui in Song territory, took the stockades of Gaoyang, Kui, and Wu, and captured defenders Yan Gui, Dou Shizhong, and Zhao Xing. A bridge across the river severed Song communications; when Song forces came to dispute it, they were driven back.

sentences.zh: 還攻牛頭城，以火箭焚其官舍民居。

translations.literal: Returning, he attacked Niutou City and burned its official halls and dwellings with fire-arrows.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he assaulted Niutou City and set its halls and houses ablaze with fire-arrows.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣蔡邦光略九君山，擒其將孫德、柳榮、趙威。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent Cai Bangguang to raid Jiujun Mountain and captured the generals Sun De, Liu Rong, and Zhao Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Cai Bangguang against Jiujun Mountain and captured the generals Sun De, Liu Rong, and Zhao Wei.

sentences.zh: 時宋以鮮汝忠、趙章易鎮開、達二州，而汝忠家屬尚留開。

translations.literal: At that time the Song replaced the garrisons of Kai and Da with Xian Ruzhong and Zhao Zhang, while Ruzhong's family remained in Kai.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had reassigned Kai and Da to Xian Ruzhong and Zhao Zhang, though Ruzhong's household still remained in Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 文安曰：「達未易攻，若先拔開州，俘其家屬，以招汝忠，則達可不煩兵而下矣。」

translations.literal: Wen'an said: 'Da is not easy to attack; if we first take Kai and hold his family as hostages to summon Ruzhong, Da may fall without troubling the army.'
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an said: 'Dazhou is hard to storm. If we first take Kaizhou and hold his family to summon Ruzhong, Dazhou may submit without a prolonged campaign.'

sentences.zh: 乃遣蔡邦光率千戶呼延順等，往攻開州，而盛兵駐蟠龍，以為聲援。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent Cai Bangguang with the chiliarchs Huyan Shun and others to attack Kai while massing troops at Panlong as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cai Bangguang with the chiliarchs Huyan Shun and others against Kaizhou while concentrating a large force at Panlong as reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，諸軍夜銜枚，薄開州城下，遣死士先登，斬關以入，及城中人知，則千戶景疇已立旗幟于城之絕頂矣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year all troops advanced at night with gags in their mouths and closed on Kai below the walls; assault troops scaled first, cut the gate-bar, and entered—and by the time those in the city knew it, the chiliarch Jing Chou had already raised banners on the summit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year the armies moved at night with gags in their mouths and pressed to the walls of Kaizhou. Assault teams scaled first, cut the bar, and broke in; before the garrison knew it, Chiliarch Jing Chou had planted his standard on the highest point.

sentences.zh: 宋軍潰散，擒趙章，而守將韓明父子猶率所部兵巷戰，力屈，亦就擒。

translations.literal: The Song army scattered in defeat; Zhao Zhang was captured, but the defenders Han Ming, father and son, still led their troops in street fighting until exhausted, when they too surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Song force broke and scattered; Zhao Zhang was taken. The defenders Han Ming and his son still fought house to house until spent, then yielded.

sentences.zh: 文安遷汝忠家屬于蟠龍，遣元帥王師能持檄往達州招之曰：「降則家屬得全，不降則闔城塗炭，汝宜早為計。」

translations.literal: Wen'an moved Ruzhong's family to Panlong and sent Marshal Wang Shineng with a summons to Da, saying: 'Surrender and your household is spared; resist and the whole city is destroyed—consider early.'
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an relocated Ruzhong's family to Panlong and sent Marshal Wang Shineng to Dazhou with a summons: 'Submit and your household lives; hold out and the city is annihilated—choose quickly.'

sentences.zh: 汝忠遂遣趙榮來約降，王師能以兵入據其城。

translations.literal: Ruzhong thereupon sent Zhao Rong to arrange surrender; Wang Shineng entered and held the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhong then sent Zhao Rong to negotiate surrender, and Wang Shineng entered to occupy the city.

sentences.zh: 汝忠率所部將士，詣文安軍門降，悉還其妻孥財物。

translations.literal: Ruzhong led his officers and men to Wen'an's camp to surrender; all wives, children, and goods were returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ruzhong came in person with his officers and men to Wen'an's camp and submitted; wives, children, and property were all restored.

sentences.zh: 趙章子桂楫，守師姑城，遣兵招之，亦降。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhang's son Guiji held Shigu City; troops were sent to summon him, and he too surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhang's son Guiji held Shigu City; when troops were sent to receive his submission, he surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 獨洋州龍爪城守將謝益固守，併力攻之，擒統制王慶，益棄城走。

translations.literal: Only the Yang Prefecture Longzhao City defender Xie Yi held fast; attacking with combined strength, they captured Commander Wang Qing; Yi abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xie Yi at Longzhao in Yang Prefecture held out. A combined assault captured Commander Wang Qing; Yi abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是遣元帥李吉、嵇永興，千戶王新德等，將兵以鮮汝忠往招由山等處八城，皆望風迎降，凱還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Marshals Li Ji and Ji Yongxing and the chiliarch Wang Xinde and others with troops, taking Xian Ruzhong to summon the eight cities of Youshan and elsewhere; all submitted at the first report of his approach, and the army returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Marshals Li Ji and Ji Yongxing and Chiliarch Wang Xinde and others, with Xian Ruzhong, to receive the submission of eight cities including Youshan; all capitulated at his approach, and the army returned in triumph.

sentences.zh: 遣經歷陳德勝以鮮汝忠、趙桂楫等十餘人獻捷京師。

translations.literal: He sent the commissioner Chen Desheng to present Xian Ruzhong, Zhao Guiji, and more than ten others as prisoners of victory at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Commissioner Chen Desheng to the capital with Xian Ruzhong, Zhao Guiji, and more than ten others as trophies of victory.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，加授文安驃騎衛上將軍，兼宣撫使，賜鈔一千錠；

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and further appointed Wen'an General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and concurrent Pacification Commissioner, granting one thousand ingots of paper money;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased, further appointing Wen'an General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Cavalry Guard with concurrent Pacification Commissioner, and granting one thousand ingots of banknotes.

sentences.zh: 文粲加授鎮國上將軍。

translations.literal: Wencan was further appointed General of the State-Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan was further promoted to General of the State-Pacifying Army.

sentences.zh: 文安尋遣其兄子應之，往招都勝、茂竹、廣福三城，自將大軍，以為聲援，皆降之。

translations.literal: Wen'an soon sent his brother's son Yingzhi to summon the three cities of Dusheng, Maozhu, and Guangfu, himself leading the main army in support; all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an soon sent his nephew Yingzhi to receive Dusheng, Maozhu, and Guangfu while he led the main army in support; all three submitted.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，兵至樂勝城，宋將蒲濟川降。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the army reached Lesheng City; the Song general Pu Jichuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the army reached Lesheng City; the Song general Pu Jichuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進攻梁山，宋將袁世安堅守。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Liangshan, the Song general Yuan Shi'an held firm.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced on Liangshan, where the Song general Yuan Shi'an defended stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 文安焚其外城，梁山軍恃忠勝軍為固，力攻拔之，殺守將王智，擒部轄景福，圍梁山四十日，世安隨方備禦，竟不降。

translations.literal: Wen'an burned the outer city; the Liangshan army relied on Zhongsheng Army as its stronghold—they attacked with force, stormed it, killed the defender Wang Zhi, captured Controller Jing Fu, and besieged Liangshan forty days while Shi'an defended on every side, yet he would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an burned the outer works. The Liangshan garrison leaned on Zhongsheng Army as its bastion; a forced assault took it, killing the defender Wang Zhi and capturing Controller Jing Fu. Liangshan was besieged forty days; Shi'an met each threat, yet would not yield.

sentences.zh: 文安乃移兵攻萬州之牛頭城，殺守將何威，遷其民，進圍萬州，守將上官夔戰守甚力。

translations.literal: Wen'an then shifted troops to attack Niutou City in Wan Prefecture, killed the defender He Wei, relocated the populace, and advanced to besiege Wan; the defender Shangguan Kui fought and defended with great vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an then moved against Niutou City in Wanzhou, killed the defender He Wei, relocated the inhabitants, and pressed the siege of Wanzhou, where Shangguan Kui resisted with fierce determination.

sentences.zh: 文安乃遣監軍楊應之、鎮撫彭福壽，會東川行院兵，出小江口以牽制援兵，果與之遇，戰敗之，擒緫管李皋、花茂實等。

translations.literal: Wen'an then sent Supervisor Yang Yingzhi and Pacification Commissioner Peng Fushou to join Eastern Chuan Branch Secretariat troops, issuing from Xiaojiangkou to tie down relief forces; they indeed met them, defeated them in battle, and captured Supervisors Li Gao, Hua Maoshi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an sent Supervisor Yang Yingzhi and Pacification Commissioner Peng Fushou with Eastern Chuan Branch Secretariat troops out from Xiaojiangkou to pin down relief columns. They met the enemy as expected, defeated them, and captured Supervisors Li Gao, Hua Maoshi, and others.

sentences.zh: 萬州固守不下，文安乃解圍去。

translations.literal: Wan Prefecture held firm and could not be taken; Wen'an thereupon raised the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhou would not yield; Wen'an lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 攻石城堡，諭降守將譚汝和；

translations.literal: They attacked Shicheng Fort and persuaded the defender Tan Ruhe to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted Shicheng Fort and induced the defender Tan Ruhe to submit;

sentences.zh: 攻雞冠城，諭降守將杜賦；

translations.literal: they attacked Jiguan City and persuaded the defender Du Fu to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: they took Jiguan City and induced Du Fu to surrender;

sentences.zh: 又招石馬、鐵平、小城、三聖、油木、牟家、下隘等城。

translations.literal: and again received the submission of the cities of Shima, Tieping, Xiaocheng, Sansheng, Youmu, Moujia, and Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: and also received the submission of Shima, Tieping, Xiaocheng, Sansheng, Youmu, Moujia, Xiayi, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 冬，進白帝城，夔帥張起巖堅守不出，文安以師老，乃還。

translations.literal: In winter they advanced on Baidi City; the Kui commander Zhang Qiyan held firm and would not come out. Wen'an, because the army was weary, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they advanced on Baidi City. The Kui commander Zhang Qiyan held fast and refused to sally. With his troops exhausted, Wen'an withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宋都統弋德復據開州，文安乃築城神仙山以逼之，令元帥蔡邦光、萬戶紀天英屯守。

translations.literal: The Song commander-in-chief Yi De again held Kai Prefecture; Wen'an then built a city on Shenxian Mountain to press him and ordered Marshals Cai Bangguang and the myriarch Ji Tianying to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander Yi De reoccupied Kaizhou. Wen'an built a fortress on Shenxian Mountain to threaten him and stationed Marshals Cai Bangguang and Myriarch Ji Tianying there.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進階金吾衛上將軍，賜玉帶一。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to General of the Upper Army of the Golden Crow Guard and granted one jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to General of the Upper Army of the Golden Crow Guard and given a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 夏，朝廷遣安西王相李德輝經畫東川課程，宋梁山守將袁世安遣使約降。

translations.literal: In summer the court sent the Anxi King's minister Li Dehui to organize the Eastern Chuan revenue program; the Song Liangshan defender Yuan Shi'an sent envoys to arrange surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the court sent Li Dehui, minister to the Anxi Prince, to arrange Eastern Chuan revenues. The Song defender of Liangshan, Yuan Shi'an, sent envoys to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 文安以白德輝，德輝大喜，即遣文安將兵，奉王旨往招之，世安遂降。

translations.literal: Wen'an reported this to Dehui; Dehui was greatly pleased and immediately sent Wen'an with troops, bearing the prince's order to summon him, and Shi'an thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an informed Dehui, who was delighted and at once sent Wen'an with troops under the prince's commission to receive him; Shi'an submitted.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，進軍攻萬州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the army advanced to attack Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the army marched against Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣經歷徐政諭守臣上官夔降，夔不從，圍之數匝，踰月，攻拔外城。

translations.literal: He sent the commissioner Xu Zheng to urge the defending minister Shangguan Kui to surrender; Kui would not comply. They besieged it several deep; after more than a month they stormed the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xu Zheng was sent to urge the defender Shangguan Kui to yield; Kui refused. The siege ringed the city severalfold; after more than a month the outer walls fell.

sentences.zh: 夔守張起巖來救，遣鎮撫彭福壽迎擊，破之，盡殺其舟師，俘其將宋明。

translations.literal: Kui's defender Zhang Qiyan came to relieve; he sent Pacification Commissioner Peng Fushou to meet and attack, defeated him, killed all his boat troops, and captured his general Song Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiyan came to relieve the siege. Wen'an sent Pacification Commissioner Peng Fushou to intercept, routed him, destroyed his river force, and captured the general Song Ming.

sentences.zh: 萬州奪氣，文安復傳王旨，諭夔使降，夔終不屈。

translations.literal: Wan Prefecture lost its spirit; Wen'an again transmitted the prince's order urging Kui to surrender, but Kui to the end would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhou's morale collapsed. Wen'an again conveyed the prince's summons for Kui to surrender, but Kui would not bend.

sentences.zh: 文安盡銳攻城，潛遣勇士梯城宵登，斬關而入，夔巷戰而死。

translations.literal: Wen'an attacked the city with all his elite; secretly he sent brave men to scale the walls by night on ladders, cut the bar, and enter; Kui died fighting in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an threw his best troops at the walls. By night assault teams scaled the ramparts, cut the gate-bar, and broke in; Kui fell fighting in the alleys.

sentences.zh: 萬州既定，遣使招鐵檠、三寶兩城守將楊宜、黎拱辰降，分兵略施州，擒統制薛忠，會大雪，遣蔡邦光夜攻，殺守帥何艮，奪其城。

translations.literal: When Wan Prefecture was settled, he sent envoys to summon the defenders of Tiejing and Sanbao, Yang Yi and Li Gongchen, to surrender; he divided troops to raid Shi Prefecture and captured Commander Xue Zhong. Heavy snow fell; he sent Cai Bangguang to attack by night, killed the defending commander He Gen, and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: With Wanzhou secured, he summoned the defenders of Tiejing and Sanbao, Yang Yi and Li Gongchen, to submit. Detached columns raided Shizhou and took Commander Xue Zhong. In heavy snow Cai Bangguang attacked by night, killed the commander He Gen, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏，進兵攻咸淳府，時宋以六郡鎮撫使馬堃為守，文安與堃同里閈，諭之使降，堃不從，乃列柵攻城。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year he advanced to attack Xianchun Prefecture. At that time the Song had appointed the Six-Circuit Pacification Commissioner Ma Kun as defender; Wen'an, being from the same neighborhood as Kun, urged him to surrender, but Kun would not comply, and they therefore set palisades to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourteenth year he advanced on Xianchun Prefecture. The Song had made Ma Kun, Pacification Commissioner of six circuits, its defender. A fellow townsman, Wen'an urged him to submit; Kun refused, and palisades were raised for the siege.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，潛遣勇士躡雲梯宵登，斬關納外兵，堃悉力巷戰，達州安撫使鮮汝忠與宋兵力戰死，比曉，宋兵大敗，堃力屈就擒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter, secretly sending brave men to mount cloud-ladders and scale by night, they cut the bar and admitted the outer troops. Kun fought with all his strength in the streets; the Da Prefecture Pacification Commissioner Xian Ruzhong and Song troops fought fiercely and died. By dawn the Song army was utterly defeated; Kun, exhausted, was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month assault teams scaled the walls on cloud-ladders by night, cut the bar, and let the outer force in. Kun fought house to house. The Dazhou Pacification Commissioner Xian Ruzhong and Song troops battled to the death. By dawn the Song force was shattered; Kun, spent, was taken.

sentences.zh: 十五年，進兵攻紹慶，守將鮮龍迎敵。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he advanced to attack Shaoqing; the defender Xian Long came out to meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he marched on Shaoqing; the defender Xian Long marched out to engage.

sentences.zh: 二月，潛遣勇士，夜以梯衝攻破其北門，鮮龍大驚，收散卒力戰，兵敗就擒。

translations.literal: In the second month, secretly sending brave men to break the north gate by night with ladder-rams, Xian Long was greatly alarmed, gathered scattered troops and fought with all his strength; the army was defeated and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month night assault teams broke the north gate with battering ladders. Xian Long, startled, rallied scattered men and fought desperately until defeated and captured.

sentences.zh: 蜀境已定，獨夔堅守不下。

translations.literal: The Shu territory was now settled; only Kui still held firm and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was largely pacified; only Kui still held out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命荊湖都元帥達海，由巫峽進兵取夔州，而西川劉僉院，挾夔守將親屬往招之。

translations.literal: The court ordered the Jing-Hu supreme commander Dahai to take Kui Prefecture by advancing through the Wu Gorge, while the Western Chuan Commissioner Liu took the Kui defender's kin as hostages to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Jing-Hu supreme commander Dahai to take Kuizhou through the Wu Gorge, while Western Chuan Commissioner Liu used the defender's kin to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 文安乃遣元帥王師能，將舟師與俱，張起巖竟以城降。

translations.literal: Wen'an then sent Marshal Wang Shineng with a fleet to join them, and Zhang Qiyan finally surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an sent Marshal Wang Shineng with river forces to join them, and Zhang Qiyan at last surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 夏，入覲，文安以所得城邑繪圖以獻，帝勞之曰：「汝攻城略地之功，何若是多也！」

translations.literal: In summer he came to audience; Wen'an presented maps of the cities he had taken. The Emperor comforted him, saying: 'Your merit in storming cities and seizing territory—how can there be so much of it!'
translations.idiomatic: In summer he presented himself at court and offered maps of the cities he had won. The Emperor praised him: 'Your conquests in storming cities and seizing territory—how can there be so many!'

sentences.zh: 擢四川南道宣慰使，解白貂裘以賜之。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Southern Sichuan Route and given a white sable coat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner of the Southern Sichuan Route and granted a white sable fur coat.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遣辯士王介諭降散毛諸洞蠻，以散毛兩子入覲，因進言曰：「元帥蔡邦光，昔征散毛蠻而死，可念也。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he sent the debater Wang Jie to urge the Sanmao cave barbarians of various districts to submit; because the two sons of Sanmao came to audience, he further said: 'Marshal Cai Bangguang died in the past campaign against the Sanmao barbarians—this should be remembered.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he sent Wang Jie to receive the submission of the Sanmao cave tribes. When Sanmao's two sons came to court, he added: 'Marshal Cai Bangguang died campaigning against the Sanmao tribes—he should be remembered.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「散毛既降而殺之，其何以懷遠！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'Sanmao had already submitted and then was killed—how can distant peoples be won by such means!'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: 'They had submitted and were then killed—how can we win distant peoples that way!'

sentences.zh: 乃擢蔡邦光之子，陞為管軍緫管，佩虎符，賜散毛兩子金銀符各一，并賜其酋長以金虎符。

translations.literal: He thereupon promoted Cai Bangguang's son, raising him to commander-in-chief of army management with a tiger tally, granted each of Sanmao's two sons a gold and silver tally-token, and also granted the tribal chieftain a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Cai Bangguang's son to commander of army administration with a tiger tally, gave each of Sanmao's sons gold and silver tally-tokens, and granted the chieftain a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 遙授文安參知政事，行四川南道宣慰使。

translations.literal: Wen'an was appointed by distant commission as Vice Director of the Secretariat and acting Pacification Commissioner of the Southern Sichuan Route.
translations.idiomatic: Wen'an received a distant appointment as Vice Director of the Secretariat and acting Pacification Commissioner of the Southern Sichuan Route.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，入覲，擢龍虎衛上將軍、中書左丞，行江西省事，到官踰月，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year he came to audience and was promoted to General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Dragon Guard and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, administering Jiangxi affairs; after more than a month in office he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the nineteenth year he came to court and was made General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Dragon Guard and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of Jiangxi. After little more than a month in office he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子艮之，襲佩虎符、昭勇大將軍、管軍萬戶，歷湖南宣慰副使，岳州路緫管，卒。

translations.literal: His son Genzhi inherited the tiger tally as Grand General of Valiant Courage and commander of ten thousand households, served as Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hunan and Route Commander of Yue Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Genzhi inherited the tiger tally as Grand General of Valiant Courage and commander of ten thousand households, served as Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hunan and Route Commander of Yuezhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 劉整字武仲，先世京兆樊川人，徙鄧州穰城。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng, courtesy name Wuzhong, was originally from Fanchuan in Jingzhao; his family moved to Rangcheng in Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng, style Wuzhong, came originally from Fanchuan in Jingzhao; his family had moved to Rangcheng in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 整沉毅有智謀，善騎射。

translations.literal: Zheng was deep and resolute, possessed of strategy, and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was grave, resolute, and strategically minded, and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 金亂，入宋，隸荊湖制置使孟珙麾下。

translations.literal: When Jin fell into disorder he entered Song service and was attached to the staff of the Jing-Hu Commissioner Meng Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin realm collapsed he entered Song service under the Jing-Hu Commissioner Meng Gong.

sentences.zh: 珙攻金信陽，整為前鋒，夜縱驍勇十二人，渡塹登城，襲擒其守，還報。

translations.literal: When Gong attacked Xinyang in Jin territory, Zheng served as vanguard; by night he led twelve picked horsemen across the moat, scaled the wall, and seized the defender in a surprise attack, then returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: In Gong's assault on Jin Xinyang, Zheng led the vanguard. By night he took twelve picked riders across the ditch, scaled the wall, and seized the defender in a surprise raid, then reported back.

sentences.zh: 珙大驚，以為唐李存孝率十八騎拔洛陽，今整所將更寡，而取信陽，乃書其旗曰賽存孝。

translations.literal: Gong was greatly astonished, thinking that when Tang's Li Cunxiao with eighteen riders took Luoyang, what Zheng now led was even fewer yet he took Xinyang; he therefore wrote on his banner 'Surpassing Cunxiao.'
translations.idiomatic: Gong marveled, comparing him to Tang's Li Cunxiao, who with eighteen horsemen stormed Luoyang—yet Zheng had fewer men and took Xinyang. He inscribed Zheng's banner: Surpassing Cunxiao.

sentences.zh: 累遷潼川十五軍州安撫使，知瀘州軍州事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Pacification Commissioner of the Fifteen Armies of Tong Prefecture and Military Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Pacification Commissioner of the Fifteen Armies of Tongchuan and Military Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 整以北方人，扞西邊有功，南方諸將皆出其下，呂文德忌之，所畫策輒擯沮，有功輒掩而不白，以俞興與整有隙，使之制置四川以圖整。

translations.literal: Because Zheng was a northerner who had distinguished himself on the western frontier, the southern generals were all beneath him; Lü Wende envied him, repeatedly thwarting his plans and concealing his achievements without reporting them. Because Yu Xing bore a grudge against Zheng, he was made Commissioner of Sichuan to undermine him.
translations.idiomatic: A northerner with merit on the western frontier, Zheng outranked the southern commanders. Lü Wende envied him, blocked his plans, and suppressed reports of his victories. Yu Xing, who bore a grudge, was made Sichuan Commissioner to undermine him.

sentences.zh: 興以軍事召整，不行，遂誣搆之，整遣使訴臨安，又不得達。

translations.literal: Xing summoned Zheng on military business; Zheng would not go, and Xing thereupon framed false charges against him. Zheng sent envoys to appeal at Lin'an but they could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xing summoned him on military business; Zheng refused to come and was falsely accused. His envoys to Lin'an never reached the court.

sentences.zh: 及向士璧、曹世雄二將見殺，整益危不自保，乃謀款附。

translations.literal: When the two generals Xiang Shibi and Cao Shixiong were killed, Zheng felt ever more endangered and unable to protect himself, and thereupon planned to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: After the generals Xiang Shibi and Cao Shixiong were killed, Zheng saw that he could not survive and resolved to defect.

sentences.zh: 中統二年夏，整籍瀘州十五郡、戶三十萬入附。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Zhongtong, Zheng registered the fifteen commanderies of Luzhou and three hundred thousand households in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhongtong year 2, Zheng offered the fifteen prefectures of Luzhou and three hundred thousand households in submission.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其來，授夔府行省，兼安撫使，賜金虎符，仍賜金銀符以給其將校之有功者。

translations.literal: The Founder was pleased at his coming and appointed him to the Kui Prefecture Branch Secretariat with concurrent Pacification Commissioner, granting a gold tiger tally and also gold and silver tally-tokens for his meritorious officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder welcomed his submission, appointed him to the Kuifu Branch Secretariat as Pacification Commissioner, granted a gold tiger tally, and gave gold and silver tally-tokens to his meritorious officers.

sentences.zh: 俞興攻瀘州，整出寶器分士卒，激使戰，戰數十合，敗之。

translations.literal: Yu Xing attacked Luzhou; Zheng brought out precious vessels to divide among the troops, rousing them to fight; after several dozen engagements he defeated Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xing attacked Luzhou. Zheng distributed treasure among the ranks to stir them to battle and, after dozens of engagements, defeated him.

sentences.zh: 復遣使以宋所賜金字牙符及佩印入獻，請益屯兵、厚儲積為圖宋計。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys presenting the gold-character tally and seal bestowed by Song, requesting additional garrison troops and ample stores for a plan against Song.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent envoys with the gold-character tally and seal the Song had given him, asking for more troops and stores to plan the conquest of Song.

sentences.zh: 三年，入朝，授行中書省於成都、潼川兩路，賜銀萬兩，分給軍士之失業者，仍兼都元帥，立寨諸山，以扼宋兵。

translations.literal: In the third year he came to court and was appointed to a Branch Secretariat over the Chengdu and Tongchuan routes, granted ten thousand taels of silver to distribute to soldiers who had lost their livelihoods, and still held the post of supreme commander, establishing stockades on various mountains to block Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to court, was given a Branch Secretariat over Chengdu and Tongchuan, ten thousand taels of silver for unemployed soldiers, and retained supreme command, building stockades in the hills to block the Song.

sentences.zh: 同列嫉整功，將謀陷之，整懼，請分帥潼川。

translations.literal: Colleagues envied Zheng's achievements and were about to plot against him; Zheng was afraid and requested to divide command of Tongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues envied his success and plotted against him; in fear he asked to command Tongchuan separately.

sentences.zh: 七月，改潼川都元帥，宣課茶鹽以餉軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was changed to supreme commander of Tongchuan, levying tea and salt revenues to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he became supreme commander of Tongchuan, with tea and salt revenues assigned to feed his troops.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，宋安撫高達、溫和，進逼成都，整馳援之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year the Song Pacification Commissioners Gao Da and Wen He advanced pressing on Chengdu; Zheng galloped to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year the Song commissioners Gao Da and Wen He pressed Chengdu; Zheng rode hard to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 宋兵聞賽存孝至，遁去，將擣潼川，又與整遇于錦江而敗。

translations.literal: When the Song army heard that 'Surpassing Cunxiao' had come, they fled; intending to strike Tongchuan, they again met Zheng on the Jin River and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Surpassing Cunxiao had arrived, the Song force fled. Marching on Tongchuan, they met Zheng on the Jin River and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 至元三年六月，遷昭武大將軍、南京路宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to Grand General of Illustrious Might and Pacification Commissioner of Nanjing Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhiyuan year 3 he was made Grand General of Illustrious Might and Pacification Commissioner of the Nanjing Route.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，入朝，進言：「宋主弱臣悖，立國一隅，今天啟混一之機。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year he came to court and advanced counsel: 'The Song ruler is weak and his ministers rebellious; the state stands in a corner of the realm—today Heaven opens the opportunity for unification.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year he came to court and said: 'The Song sovereign is weak and his ministers disloyal; the state clings to one corner of the empire—Heaven now offers the moment for unification.

sentences.zh: 臣願效犬馬勞，先攻襄陽，撤其扞蔽。」

translations.literal: I wish to exert myself like a dog or horse, first attacking Xiangyang and removing its shield.'
translations.idiomatic: I am ready to serve like a hound or horse, first striking Xiangyang and stripping away its shield.'

sentences.zh: 廷議沮之。

translations.literal: Court discussion obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated and blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 整又曰：「自古帝王，非四海一家，不為正統。

translations.literal: Zheng again said: 'From antiquity emperors—unless all within the four seas are one family, they are not orthodox rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng added: 'From antiquity, no emperor has been orthodox unless the four seas are one family.

sentences.zh: 聖朝有天下十七八，何置一隅不問，而自棄正統邪！」

translations.literal: The sage dynasty already holds seven or eight parts of the empire—why leave one corner unattended and abandon orthodoxy yourself!'
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty already holds seven or eight parts of the realm—why ignore one corner and abandon our own orthodoxy!'

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「朕意決矣。」

translations.literal: The Founder said: 'My mind is decided.'
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said: 'My decision is made.'

sentences.zh: 五年七月，遷鎮國上將軍、都元帥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, seventh month, he was transferred to General of the State-Pacifying Army and supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fifth year he was made General of the State-Pacifying Army and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 九月，偕都元帥阿朮督諸軍，圍襄陽，城鹿門堡及白河口，為攻取計，率兵五萬，鈔略沿江諸郡，皆嬰城避其銳，俘人民八萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, together with the supreme commander Azhu, he supervised the armies in besieging Xiangyang, building Lumen Fort and Baikou Ford for the plan of capture, leading fifty thousand troops to raid along the river commanderies; all shut their cities to avoid his edge, and eighty thousand people were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he joined Supreme Commander Azhu in besieging Xiangyang, built Lumen Fort and Baikou Ford, led fifty thousand men to raid river districts—all walled up before his spear—and took eighty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，擒都統唐永堅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year he captured the commander-in-chief Tang Yongjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year he captured Commander-in-Chief Tang Yongjian.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，築實心臺于漢水中流，上置弩砲，下為石囤五，以扼敵船。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year he built a solid platform in midstream on the Han River, mounting crossbows and catapults above and five stone bins below to block enemy ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventh year he built a solid platform midstream on the Han, with crossbows and catapults above and five stone bins below to choke enemy shipping.

sentences.zh: 且與阿朮計曰：「我精兵突騎，所當者破，惟水戰不如宋耳。

translations.literal: He also said to Azhu: 'Our picked troops and charging cavalry break all they meet—only in naval fighting we are not equal to Song.
translations.idiomatic: He told Azhu: 'Our elite horse and shock cavalry shatter all before them—only on water we are not Song's match.

sentences.zh: 奪彼所長，造戰艦，習水軍，則事濟矣。」

translations.literal: Seize what they excel at—build war junks and train a navy—then the affair will succeed.'
translations.idiomatic: Take their strength from them: build war junks and drill a navy, and the task will be done.'

sentences.zh: 乘驛以聞，制可。

translations.literal: He took the post road to report; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reported by post courier; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 既還，造船五千艘，日練水軍，雖雨不能出，亦畫地為船而習之，得練卒七萬。

translations.literal: On his return he built five thousand vessels and daily drilled the navy; even when rain kept them indoors they traced ships on the ground to practice, obtaining seventy thousand trained soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he built five thousand ships and drilled the navy daily; when rain kept men ashore they traced ships on the ground. He trained seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 八月，復築外圍，以遏敵援。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he again built an outer encirclement to block enemy relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he built an outer ring of fortifications to cut off relief.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，宋帥范文虎遣都統張順、張貴，駕輪船，饋襄陽衣甲，邀擊，斬順，獨貴得入城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year the Song commander Fan Wenhui sent commanders-in-chief Zhang Shun and Zhang Gui in paddle-wheel ships bearing armor and supplies for Xiangyang; they intercepted them, beheaded Shun, and Gui alone entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year Fan Wenhui sent Zhang Shun and Zhang Gui in paddle-wheel ships with armor and supplies for Xiangyang. They intercepted and killed Shun; only Gui reached the city.

sentences.zh: 九月，陞參知河南行中書省事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was promoted to Vice Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was promoted Vice Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，加諸翼漢軍都元帥。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he was made supreme commander of all Han army wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he was made supreme commander of all Han army contingents.

sentences.zh: 襄陽帥呂文煥登城觀敵，整躍馬前曰：「君昧於天命，害及生靈，豈仁者之事！

translations.literal: The Xiangyang commander Lü Wenhuan mounted the wall to observe the enemy; Zheng spurred his horse forward and said: 'You are blind to Heaven's mandate and harm living people—is this the act of the humane!
translations.idiomatic: Commander Lü Wenhuan watched from the wall. Zheng rode forward: 'You ignore Heaven's mandate and harm the people—is that humane?

sentences.zh: 而又齷齪不能戰，取羞於勇者，請與君決勝負。」

translations.literal: Moreover you are petty and cannot fight, bringing shame on the brave—let us settle it in single combat.'
translations.idiomatic: You are too craven to fight and disgrace the valiant—meet me in single combat.'

sentences.zh: 文煥不荅，伏弩中整。

translations.literal: Wenhuan did not answer; a hidden crossbow bolt struck Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan did not reply; a hidden crossbow bolt hit Zheng.

sentences.zh: 三月，破樊城外郭，斬首二千級，擒裨將十六人。

translations.literal: In the third month they broke the outer wall of Fan City, beheading two thousand and capturing sixteen deputy commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they breached Fan City's outer wall, taking two thousand heads and sixteen deputy commanders.

sentences.zh: 諜知文煥將遣張貴出城求援，乃分部戰艦，縛草如牛狀，傍漢水，綿亙參錯，衆莫測所用，九月，貴果夜出，乘輪船，順流下走，軍士覘知之，傍岸爇草牛如晝，整與阿朮麾戰艦，轉戰五十里，擒貴于櫃門關，餘衆盡殺之。

translations.literal: Learning by espionage that Wenhuan would send Zhang Gui out of the city to seek relief, they divided the war fleet and bound straw in the shape of oxen along the Han, stretching them in confusion so none could tell their use. In the ninth month Gui indeed came out by night in paddle-wheel ships fleeing downstream; the soldiers detected it and burned the straw oxen along the bank bright as day. Zheng and Azhu commanded the war fleet, fighting fifty li, and captured Gui at Guimen Pass; the rest were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported Wenhuan would send Zhang Gui for relief. They divided the fleet and lined the Han with straw oxen in tangled array so none could guess their purpose. In the ninth month Gui slipped out by night in paddle-wheel ships downstream. Scouts lit the straw oxen along the bank till daybreak. Zheng and Azhu led the fleet fifty li, captured Gui at Guimen Pass, and killed the rest.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔統水軍四萬戶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month an edict placed him in command of forty thousand naval households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict gave him command of forty thousand naval households.

sentences.zh: 宋荊湖制置李庭芝以金印牙符，授整漢軍都元帥、盧龍軍節度使，封燕郡王，為書，使永寧僧持送整所，期以間整。

translations.literal: The Song Jing-Hu Commissioner Li Tingzhi, with a gold seal and tally, appointed Zheng supreme commander of the Han armies and Military Commissioner of Lulong, enfeoffed him as Prince of Yan, wrote a letter, and had a Yongning monk carry it to Zheng's camp, intending to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Song Commissioner Li Tingzhi sent a gold seal and tally making Zheng Han supreme commander and Lulong Military Commissioner, enfeoffing him Prince of Yan, with a letter carried by a Yongning monk to sow discord.

sentences.zh: 永寧令得之，驛以聞于朝，敕張易、姚樞雜問，適整至自軍，言宋怒臣畫策攻襄陽，故設此以殺臣，臣實不知。

translations.literal: The Yongning magistrate obtained it and reported by post to court; the Emperor ordered Zhang Yi and Yao Shu to question him jointly. Zheng had just come from the army and said Song was enraged that he had planned the Xiangyang attack and therefore set this trap to kill him—he truly knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongning magistrate seized it and reported by courier. Zhang Yi and Yao Shu were ordered to interrogate him. Zheng had just arrived from camp and said the Song, furious at his Xiangyang strategy, fabricated this to destroy him—he knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 詔令整復書謂：「整受命以來，惟知督厲戎兵，舉垂亡孤城耳。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zheng to reply in a letter: 'Since receiving my commission I have known only to urge and discipline the troops and raise this nearly fallen lone city.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Zheng reply: 'Since I took command I have done nothing but drive the troops and press this dying lone fortress.

sentences.zh: 宋若果以生靈為念，當重遣信使，請命朝廷，顧為此小數，何益於事！」

translations.literal: If Song truly cares for the people, it should send trusted envoys again to beg mercy of the court—what good are such petty tricks!'
translations.idiomatic: If Song truly cares for the people, let it send envoys to beg the court's mercy—what use are such petty stratagems!'

sentences.zh: 時圍襄陽已五年，整計樊、襄唇齒也，宜先攻樊城。

translations.literal: At that time the siege of Xiangyang had lasted five years; Zheng judged that Fan and Xiang were lip and teeth and that Fan City should be attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Xiangyang had lasted five years. Zheng judged Fan and Xiang interdependent and that Fan City must be taken first.

sentences.zh: 樊城人以柵蔽城，斬木列置江中，貫以鐵索。

translations.literal: The people of Fan City used palisades to screen the wall, felled trees set in the river, and threaded them with iron chains.
translations.idiomatic: Fan City's defenders screened the walls with palisades, sank felled timbers in the river, and chained them with iron.

sentences.zh: 整言於丞相伯顏，令善水者斷木沉索，督戰艦趨城下，以回回砲擊之，而焚其柵。

translations.literal: Zheng said to the Chancellor Bayan: have skilled swimmers cut the timbers and sink the chains, urge the war fleet to the foot of the wall, bombard with Muslim catapults, and burn the palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng told Chancellor Bayan to send swimmers to cut the timbers and sink the chains, drive the fleet to the wall, batter it with Muslim catapults, and burn the palisades.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，遂破樊城，屠之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year they thereupon broke Fan City and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year they stormed Fan City and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 遣唐永堅入襄陽，諭呂文煥，乃以城降。

translations.literal: They sent Tang Yongjian into Xiangyang to urge Lü Wenhuan, and he thereupon surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Tang Yongjian into Xiangyang to urge Lü Wenhuan, who then surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 上功，賜整田宅、金幣、良馬。

translations.literal: Merit was reported upward; Zheng was granted fields, houses, gold, coins, and fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was reported; he received estates, gold, coin, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 整入朝，奏曰：「襄陽破，則臨安搖矣。

translations.literal: Zheng came to court and memorialized: 'When Xiangyang falls, Lin'an will tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng came to court and said: 'Once Xiangyang falls, Lin'an will shake.

sentences.zh: 若將所練水軍，乘勝長驅，長江必皆非宋所有。」

translations.literal: If the navy I have trained is sent in victory to drive far, the Yangtze will no longer belong to Song.'
translations.idiomatic: If the navy I have trained presses the advantage downriver, the Yangtze will no longer be Song's.'

sentences.zh: 遂改行淮西樞密院事，駐正陽，夾淮而城，南逼江，斷其東西衝。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon changed to administer the Huai-West Military Commission, garrisoned at Zhengyang, built cities on both banks of the Huai, pressed south toward the river, and cut its east-west communications.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to the Huai-West Military Commission, stationed at Zhengyang, fortified both banks of the Huai, pressed the river line, and severed east-west communications.

sentences.zh: 十一年，陞驃騎衛上將軍、行中書左丞，宋夏貴悉水軍來攻，破之于大人洲。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; the Song Xia Gui led all his naval forces to attack and was defeated at Daren Isle.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Cavalry Guard and acting Left Vice Director. Song commander Xia Gui led the full navy against him and was beaten at Daren Isle.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，詔整別將兵出淮南，整銳欲渡江，首將止之，不果行。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year an edict ordered Zheng separately to lead troops out of Huainan; Zheng was eager to cross the river, but the supreme commander stopped him and the crossing did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year he was ordered to lead a separate force into Huainan. Eager to cross the Yangtze, he was stopped by the supreme commander and never crossed.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏入鄂，捷至，整失聲曰：「首帥止我，顧使我成功後人，善作者不必善成，果然！」

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan entered E Prefecture and victory was reported, Zheng cried out: 'The supreme commander stopped me, yet let others finish my success after me—those who plan well need not finish well—indeed!'
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan took E Prefecture and victory arrived, Zheng exclaimed: 'The supreme commander held me back so others could reap what I sowed—good planners need not be good finishers—so it proves!'

sentences.zh: 其夕，憤惋而卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: " That evening, resentful and grieved, he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening, bitter and aggrieved, he died at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈龍虎衛上將軍、中書右丞，諡武敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Dragon Guard and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the posthumous title Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Upper Army of the Valiant Dragon Guard and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Wumin.

sentences.zh: 子垣，嘗從父戰敗昝萬壽于通泉；

translations.literal: His son Yuan had followed his father in defeating Zan Wanshou at Tongquan;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan had followed him in defeating Zan Wanshou at Tongquan;

sentences.zh: 埏，管軍萬戶；

translations.literal: Yan, commander of ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Yan was commander of ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 均，榷茶提舉；

translations.literal: Jun, Commissioner for the Tea Monopoly;
translations.idiomatic: Jun was Commissioner for the Tea Monopoly;

sentences.zh: 垓，都元帥。

translations.literal: Gai, supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 孫九人，克仁，知房州。

translations.literal: He had nine grandsons; Keren was Prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine grandsons; Keren served as prefect of Fangzhou.
